To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ICM of the early mouse embryo irreversibly commits to EPI and PrE lineages in a highly dynamic manner.

Nanog expression is heterogeneous in the mouse blastocyst, that this heterogeneity is irreversible, and that the EPI and PrE lineages are not stochastic but rather are regulated by a mechanism that is currently unknown.
Nanog expression heterogeneities drive stable commitment to the EPI lineage in the mouse blastocyst.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the embryo makes the transition from totipotency to pluripotency.
understanding how pluripotent stem cells are established in the mammalian embryo, with a focus on the mouse blastocyst.
understanding how the mammalian embryo forms and how this process can be manipulated to generate stem cells and tissues for regenerative medicine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Nanog expression in the ICM is not stochastic and that it is a marker for EPI/PrEM progenitor cells.
Nanog is a marker of EPI/PrEM lineage, and that it is not a marker of the ICM.
Nanog expression is not a stochastic process in the mouse blastocyst.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heterogeneities in NanOG expression drive stable commitment to pluripotency in mouse embryos.
the ICM is a highly heterogeneous cell population, with cells expressing Nanog at varying levels.
the ICM of the blastocysts is a heterogeneous population, and that heterogeneity in Nanog expression drives commitment to the EPI lineage, which is the founder of all somatic cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the dynamic fluctuations of expression that have been observed in embryonic stem cells, the ICM of the mouse blastocyst is a highly robust system.
the EPI/PrEM lineage commitment is a highly stable and irreversible process in vivo, and that the EPI is the only cell type that can give rise to the entire embryo.
cell fate choice in the mouse blastocyst is irreversible.
